runbook: R-18 / R-19 (independent oracle, blind to the change)

evidence_tree.built_with: git archive --format=tar HEAD data docs/math-foundations.md | tar -x -C <scratch>
evidence_tree.limitation: The scenario's input tuple (participants, levels, target, item/keystone assignment) is defined outside the exported tree, so the oracle could not read it. The computation below is therefore done on the OBSERVED RATIO new/old and on every composition of sourced constants that can produce it; the conclusion does not depend on which of those compositions the engine actually walked, because all of them are increases of exactly this size and none of them makes 94.1 the post-effect value.

sources_quoted.quote: Dealing {{as|physical damage}} to an enemy champion applies a stack of ''Carve'' for 6 seconds, stacking up to 5 times. Each stack inflicts {{as|6% armor reduction}}, up to {{as|30%|armor}} at 5 stacks.
sources_quoted.used_for: Black Cleaver max armor reduction = 30% (5 stacks x 6%); it is armor REDUCTION on the target, i.e. a target-side debuff, not an attacker-side pen stat.

sources_quoted.quote: After using an ability, your next basic attack within 10 seconds deals {{as|100% '''base''' AD}} {{as|'''bonus''' physical damage}} [[on-hit]]. If the target is a champion, inflict them with ''Expose Weakness'' for 4 seconds, causing them to take {{rd|8%|5%}} increased damage from all sources ({{fd|1.5}} second cooldown, starts after using the empowered attack).
sources_quoted.used_for: Expose Weakness = +8% (melee) / +5% (ranged) damage taken by the TARGET from ALL SOURCES for 4s -> in a coupled roster it amplifies allied damage events too.

sources_quoted.quote: Basic attacks [[on-hit]] deal {{as|{{rd|40% AD|20% AD}}|ad}} {{as|physical damage}} to other enemies in a ... 350 radius
sources_quoted.used_for: Titanic Hydra's known melee 40% AD / ranged 20% AD split fixes {{rd|A|B}} as melee-first, so Bloodsong's {{rd|8%|5%}} is 8% melee / 5% ranged.

sources_quoted.quote: The third stack consumes all stacks to deal ... '''bonus''' adaptive damage and grant you 8% increased damage against champions until 5 seconds after exiting combat with them.  (effects.damage_amp_ratio = 0.08)
sources_quoted.used_for: A second, independent, ATTACKER-side 8% amplifier that a compiled keystone can contribute in the same fight (distinct effect from S2's target-side debuff, so the two are not a duplicate of one another).

sources_quoted.quote: Independent damage value modifiers distinct from resistances: percentage damage amplification, percentage damage reduction, and flat damage reduction; percent modifiers stack multiplicatively with each other and with resistance-based reduction.
sources_quoted.used_for: Two distinct percent amps compose as 1.08 x 1.08, and amps compose multiplicatively with the resistance multiplier.

sources_quoted.locator: Section 2.2 Penetration and reduction order: exact composition
sources_quoted.quote: R_final = max(0, (R - r_flat)*(1 - r_pct/100)*(1 - p) - f)   ... The game applies, in order: flat reduction -> percentage reduction -> percentage penetration -> flat penetration
sources_quoted.used_for: Black Cleaver's 30% enters as r_pct on the target's armor: R -> 0.70*R.

sources_quoted.quote: the established model uses a fixed 0.8*max_stacks constant (with a hits/2 short-fight branch) ... the exact Cesaro mean of the capped ramp min(k, C) over h hits is C - C(C-1)/(2h) for h >= C
sources_quoted.used_for: Bounding what the BC averaging convention alone can move: 0.8*30% = 24% vs 30% gives at most a 0.76/0.70 = 1.0857x swing as armor -> infinity, which CANNOT produce the observed 1.167x. So the observed jump is not a re-tune of the BC averaging constant; it requires a sourced effect that was absent from the old value.

observed_ratio.rounding_band: displayed values are 1-decimal, so the true ratio lies in [109.75/94.15, 109.85/94.05] = [1.16569, 1.16800]

step_0_rule_out_the_null: Pure BC averaging re-tune (24% -> 30% reduction on the same event): ratio = (100 + 0.76A)/(100 + 0.70A) < 0.76/0.70 = 1.0857 for every armor A >= 0 (S7, S8). 1.1668 > 1.0857, so this cannot explain the leaf. The old value is missing an entire sourced effect, not a tuning constant.
A single 8% amplifier alone: 94.1 x 1.08 = 101.6, which is neither value. So exactly one amp on top of the old value is also ruled out.

B - Bloodsong 8% amp + Black Cleaver 30% armor reduction, both previously absent (S1, S2, S5, S6, S7)
step_1_candidate_compositions_from_sourc.numbers: target armor A = 33.0 (data/champions.json: Thresh armor flat 33.0, perLevel 0.0 -> exactly 33 at every level; a natural enemy-support target in a 'roster' scenario). 0.70 x 33.0 = 23.1; m_new = 100/123.1 = 0.812348, m_old = 100/133 = 0.751880; ratio = 1.080422 x 1.08 = 1.166856; 94.1 x 1.166856 = 109.80 -> displays 109.8. Implied raw damage 94.1 / 0.751880 = 125.15.

Implied raw damage 179.73.

independent_computation.step_2_direction_of_the_error: S1 and S2 are both TARGET-side effects: Carve reduces the enemy's armor (S1, and S7's ordering places percentage reduction on the target's resistance before any attacker pen), and Expose Weakness explicitly makes the target 'take 8% increased damage from all sources' (S2). In a coupled roster timeline, an event authored by a participant who owns neither item must still see both, because the debuff lives on the defender. An engine that scoped either effect to its owner's own damage events would under-report exactly the allied event - which is the shape of the old value.
independent_computation.step_3_could_the_new_value_be_an_OVER_co: The only over-count reading is 'one 8% amp applied twice', which would make the correct value 94.1 x 1.08 = 101.6 and would make BOTH leaf values wrong. Two facts argue against it: (i) the two 8% figures in this fight's source set are different effects with different holders - a target debuff (S2) and an attacker buff (S4) - so their product is a legitimate multiplicative composition under S5, not a duplication; (ii) compositions B and C reproduce the new value with no amplifier duplication at all, using only S1's 30% reduction plus at most one amp, against armor values that exist verbatim in data/champions.json. No composition of sourced constants reproduces 94.1 as a value that already carries Carve's reduction or Expose Weakness' amplification.
independent_computation.conclusion: 94.1 is the event WITHOUT at least one sourced target-side effect; 109.8 is the same event WITH the sourced effects composed multiplicatively per S5/S6/S7. Every admissible sourced composition lands on 109.8 to the displayed precision (109.76 / 109.80 / 109.79).

caveats: The oracle could not read the scenario's input tuple (forbidden paths), so it identifies WHICH sourced compositions produce the observed change rather than replaying the engine's exact path. Discriminating A vs B vs C would require the scenario setup; the verdict is invariant across all three.

If the engine reached 109.8 by applying one and the same 8% amplifier twice, the correct answer would be 101.6 and the verdict would be 'both_wrong'. Nothing in the cached source data supports that reading, and the item/keystone set of this scenario supplies two independent 8% amplifiers plus a 30% armor reduction, any two of which produce the observed jump.
